law_name: Budgetsanierungsmaßnahmengesetz 2025 (Budget Consolidation Measures Act 2025), BGBl. I Nr. 7/2025
description: First consolidation package of the Stocker government, adopted by the National Council on 7 March 2025, the day the new government presented itself to Parliament. It abolished the educational leave scheme (Bildungskarenz), raised the bank levy and cut climate-related subsidies.
significance: First step of the coalition's budget consolidation, which Parliament described as the dominant theme of its first session.

law_name: Amendment to the Asylum Act 2005 (suspension of family reunification), BGBl. I Nr. 17/2025
description: Adopted by the National Council on 25 April 2025, it allows the government, with the consent of the Main Committee, to suspend family reunification for refugees and holders of subsidiary protection where public order and internal security are deemed at risk. The regulation presented by Stocker was approved on 1 July 2025 and extended in December 2025.
significance: One of the coalition's main migration measures; the FPÖ supported the regulation but called it insufficient, the Greens called it 'pure show politics on the backs of children'.

law_name: Federal Finance Acts 2025 and 2026 and Budget Accompanying Act 2025 (BGBl. I Nr. 22, 23 and 25/2025)
description: Double budget adopted by ÖVP, SPÖ and NEOS on 16–18 June 2025, with federal deficits of more than €18 billion in each year. The accompanying act, with 76 amendments, abolished the Klimabonus, tightened access to the corridor pension, froze family benefits for two years and cancelled tax relief from the 'third third' of cold-progression compensation until 2029.
significance: Did not prevent the EU from opening an excessive deficit procedure against Austria on 8 July 2025.

law_name: Amendment to the State Protection and Intelligence Service Act and related laws (messenger surveillance), BGBl. I Nr. 54/2025
description: Adopted by the National Council on 9 July 2025 by 105 votes to 71, it allows the Directorate for State Protection and Intelligence (DSN) under certain conditions to read the content of encrypted messenger communications to prevent serious attacks on the constitutional order.
significance: Opposed by the FPÖ, the Greens and two NEOS MPs on civil-liberties grounds; the Greens announced they would consider a Constitutional Court challenge.

law_name: Amendment to the Weapons Act 1996 (Waffengesetz), BGBl. I Nr. 56/2025
description: Response to the Graz school shooting of 10 June 2025, adopted by the National Council on 24 September 2025. It raised the minimum age for category B firearms from 21 to 25 and for category C from 18 to 21, introduced a longer cooling-off period and stricter psychological checks, and improved data exchange between authorities.
significance: The government's main legislative answer to the Graz shooting, in which nine young people and a teacher were killed.

law_name: 4th and 5th Rent Inflation Mitigation Acts (Mietrechtliche Inflationslinderungsgesetze), BGBl. I Nr. 12/2025 and Nr. 114/2025
description: The 4th act (7 March 2025) froze the 2025 indexation of regulated rents; the 5th (11 December 2025) capped regulated rent increases at 1% in 2026 and 2% in 2027, limited indexation for all rents above 3% inflation to half of the excess and extended minimum fixed-term leases from three to five years.
significance: The first cap on indexation that also covers free-market rents, including existing contracts.

law_name: Amendment to the School Education Act and related school laws (headscarf ban for pupils under 14), BGBl. I Nr. 117/2025
description: Adopted by the National Council on 11 December 2025 with the votes of ÖVP, SPÖ, NEOS and FPÖ. It bars girls up to their 14th birthday from wearing a headscarf 'covering the head in accordance with Islamic traditions' at public and private schools from the 2026/27 school year, with staged sanctions up to fines of €150–800, and introduces support for suspended pupils and compulsory guidance talks for school leavers.
significance: A flagship integration measure of the coalition; the Greens voted against it, calling it discriminatory and unconstitutional.

law_name: Amendment to the VAT Act 1994 (reduced 4.9% rate for basic foodstuffs), BGBl. I Nr. 37/2026
description: Adopted by the National Council on 21 May 2026, it introduced a 4.9% VAT rate for basic foods such as milk, butter, bread and eggs, previously taxed at 10%, applying since 1 July 2026.
significance: Part of the coalition's anti-inflation measures, alongside the rent brake and a fuel-price brake adopted in response to the Iran war.

law_name: Asyl- und Migrationspakt-Anpassungsgesetz (Asylum and Migration Pact Adaptation Act), BGBl. I Nr. 39/2026
description: Adopted by the National Council on 20 May 2026 to implement the EU asylum and migration pact: the admission procedure was replaced by screening and a quota system was introduced for family reunification.
significance: Turned the temporary suspension of family reunification into a permanent quota regime under EU law.

law_name: Federal Finance Acts 2027 and 2028 and Budget Accompanying Act 2027–2028 (BGBl. I Nr. 54, 55 and 62/2026)
description: Second double budget, adopted in July 2026 after five consecutive days of plenary sessions, with federal deficits of €15.5 billion (2027) and €13.2 billion (2028) and the aim of a 3% general-government deficit in 2028 to exit the EU deficit procedure. The accompanying act (68 amendments, two new laws) introduced a €2 parcel tax on large mail-order retailers, raised corporate tax to 24% on profits above €1 million, cut employers' FLAF contributions from 2028, extended the bank levy, froze many social and family benefits and set the 2027 pension increase at 2.95%.
significance: The budget framework for the rest of the legislative period, adopted with the votes of ÖVP, SPÖ and NEOS only.
